name: L.P. Grant Mansion
description: 1856 mansion, Atlanta's oldest house and HQ of the Atlanta Preservation Center; birthplace of golfer Bobby Jones and once owned by Margaret Mitchell.

name: APEX Museum
description: African American history museum on historic Sweet Auburn Avenue.

name: Atlanta Daily World Building
description: Longtime home of the Atlanta Daily World, a pioneering Black newspaper.

name: Atlanta History Center
description: 33-acre history campus with the Swan House, Smith Farm, and the Atlanta Cyclorama.

name: Balzer Theater at Herren's
description: Theater on the site of Herren's, the first Atlanta restaurant to voluntarily desegregate.

name: Wimbish House (Atlanta Woman's Club)
description: 1906 Beaux-Arts mansion, longtime home of the Atlanta Woman's Club.

name: Fulton Bag & Cotton Mill
description: 1881 textile mill, now the Cotton Mill Lofts, centerpiece of the Cabbagetown district.

name: Burns Club of Atlanta
description: Replica of Robert Burns's Scottish cottage and home of the Burns Club of Atlanta.

name: Cathedral of St. Philip
description: Large Episcopal cathedral in Buckhead.

name: Center for Puppetry Arts
description: Museum and theater devoted to puppetry, including a Jim Henson collection.

name: Historic Shoupade Park
description: Civil War 'Shoupade' fortification remnants along the Silver Comet Rail Trail.

name: MARTA Five Points Station
description: Central MARTA transit hub in downtown Atlanta.

name: East Lake Golf Club
description: Historic golf club, home course of Bobby Jones.

name: First Church of Christ, Scientist
description: Historic Midtown church.

name: First Presbyterian Church of Atlanta
description: Gothic Revival church noted for its stained glass windows and organs.

name: Swan Coach House
description: 1920s carriage house at the Atlanta History Center; restaurant and gallery.

name: The Fox Theatre
description: 1929 Moorish movie palace saved from demolition in 1975.

name: Georgia State Capitol
description: 1889 gold-domed Georgia State Capitol and Capitol Museum.

name: Glenn Memorial United Methodist Church
description: Emory-area Methodist church with a historic Little Chapel.

name: Goodrum House
description: 1929 Buckhead mansion designed by architect Philip Trammell Shutze.

name: The Healey Building
description: 1913 Gothic Revival skyscraper in the Fairlie-Poplar district.

name: Historic Oakland Cemetery
description: 1850 Victorian garden cemetery; resting place of Bobby Jones and Margaret Mitchell.

name: Sylvester Cemetery
description: Historic East Atlanta cemetery.

name: Margaret Mitchell House
description: Apartment where Margaret Mitchell wrote Gone With the Wind.

name: Museum of Contemporary Art of Georgia (MOCA GA)
description: Museum dedicated to contemporary art by Georgia artists.

name: Northside Drive Baptist Church
description: Church known for its stained glass.

name: Peachtree Christian Church
description: Gothic Revival church on Peachtree Street.

name: Piedmont Driving Club
description: Historic private social club founded in 1887.

name: Piedmont Park
description: Atlanta's signature urban park, redesigned for the 1895 Cotton States Exposition.

name: St. Anne's Episcopal Church
description: Church noted for its stained glass windows and Flentrop organ.

name: St. Mark United Methodist Church
description: Romanesque Revival church in Midtown.

name: Ivy Hall (SCAD)
description: 1883 Edward C. Peters Mansion, a Victorian landmark restored by SCAD.

name: Second-Ponce de Leon Baptist Church
description: Large historic Buckhead church.

name: Sweet Auburn Curb Market
description: 1924 municipal public market in the Sweet Auburn district.

name: The Temple
description: Historic Reform synagogue, bombed in a 1958 civil-rights-era attack.

name: The Trolley Barn
description: 1889 streetcar barn in Inman Park, now an event hall.

name: Utoy Cemetery
description: Historic cemetery on the site of the Civil War Battle of Utoy Creek.

name: Westview Cemetery
description: 1884 cemetery, one of the largest in the Southeast.

name: The Wren's Nest
description: Home of Joel Chandler Harris, author of the Uncle Remus tales, in the West End.

name: Rhodes Hall
description: 1904 Romanesque Revival 'castle on Peachtree'.

name: King Keith House
description: Queen Anne Victorian, the most-photographed 'painted lady' of Inman Park.

name: Standing Peachtree Greenspace
description: Site near Standing Peachtree, an early Creek settlement on the Chattahoochee.
